stages.name: First enclosures
stages.story: Early monumental enclosures emerge in the pre-pottery Neolithic; exact sequences differ across buildings.

stages.name: Carved pillars & gathering
stages.story: Large T-shaped pillars and circular or oval settings express elaborate communal building traditions.

stages.name: Excavated mound
stages.story: Excavations reveal portions of the enclosures; some remain covered or beneath later deposits.

caveat: Carved T-shaped pillars are observed; complete elevations and social uses remain interpretations.

stages.name: Bank, ditch & burials
stages.story: The earliest monument includes an earthwork enclosure and cremation cemetery.

stages.name: Standing stones rise
stages.story: Sarsen uprights, lintels and bluestones make Stonehenge a long-running building project.

stages.name: Surviving circle
stages.story: The standing monument is incomplete. Modern interpretation draws on archaeology and scientific dating.

caveat: Sarsens and earthworks are observed; missing stones are selectively idealized.

stages.name: Caravan landscape
stages.story: Trade routes and settled communities predate the best-known monumental facades.

stages.name: Nabataean city
stages.story: Water management and monumental rock-cut buildings flourish under Nabataean rule.

stages.name: Rock-cut remains
stages.story: Petra’s carved facades survive; the full ancient city was much larger than the famous Treasury.

caveat: A stylized cliff facade stands for Petra, not a surveyed model of Al-Khazneh.

stages.name: Andean ridge
stages.story: The steep mountain landscape predates fifteenth-century building.

stages.name: Inca royal estate
stages.story: Terraces, paths and masonry shape an Inca ceremonial and residential estate.

stages.name: Protected sanctuary
stages.story: Stonework and terraces remain in a landscape that is still home to living communities.

caveat: Terraces and buildings are schematic, not a geospatial model or exact roof reconstruction.

stages.name: Expanding Khmer capitals
stages.story: Capitals, reservoirs and temples spread across the Angkor region over centuries.

stages.name: Greater Angkor at its height
stages.story: The temples, reservoirs, fields and dispersed settlements formed a huge connected urban landscape. A research model estimates 700,000–900,000 people across Greater Angkor at its 13th-century peak, not inside Angkor Wat alone.

stages.name: Living heritage
stages.story: The temples endure through changing uses, continued cultural practice and conservation.

caveat: Angkor Wat-like towers are illustrative of one part of the larger park.

stages.name: Maya urban center
stages.story: Earlier phases of settlement and ceremonial building precede the famous surviving monuments.

stages.name: Monumental ceremonial core
stages.story: El Castillo and great civic spaces represent a complex cultural and political history.

stages.name: Conserved ruins
stages.story: Surviving stone architecture is conserved; colors and vanished buildings remain less certain.

caveat: Stepped pyramid is schematic; stages are broadly dated for storytelling.

stages.name: Urban expansion
stages.story: A planned urban system grows along the Avenue of the Dead.

stages.name: Sun & Moon pyramids
stages.story: Large pyramids and residential districts form an influential metropolis.

stages.name: Excavated avenue
stages.story: Monuments survive within a much-altered, intensively studied archaeological city.

caveat: Two pyramids and avenue are symbolic; geometry and details are not scaled.

stages.name: Hill sanctuary
stages.story: Early builders begin monumental stonework in central Java.

stages.name: Stone mandala
stages.story: Terraced galleries and bell-shaped stupas create a complex Buddhist pilgrimage space.

stages.name: Restored pilgrimage
stages.story: The monument has undergone extensive conservation and remains an active heritage site.

caveat: Concentric levels and stupas are approximations, not accurate relief galleries.

stages.name: Ancestral platforms
stages.story: Communities establish ceremonial platforms and monumental carving traditions.

stages.name: Moai on the ahu
stages.story: Moai are erected and transformed within an evolving Rapa Nui society.

stages.name: Island archaeology
stages.story: Standing and fallen figures, quarries and ceremonial sites carry distinct histories.

caveat: Moai count, posture and phase are illustrative; no universal timeline fits every ahu.

stages.name: Building islets
stages.story: Artificial islets take shape in the lagoon off Pohnpei.

stages.name: Ceremonial tidal city
stages.story: Basalt architecture and canals create a ceremonial and political center.

stages.name: Conservation challenge
stages.story: Ruins remain on tidal islets, vulnerable to water and vegetation.

caveat: Basalt-wall network is stylized; this is not a mapped canal/islet survey.

stages.name: Royal center grows
stages.story: Maya rulers build and rebuild courts, plazas and monuments.

stages.name: Classic Maya skyline
stages.story: Great temples rise above an extensive occupied city landscape.

stages.name: Forest and excavation
stages.story: Standing temples share the forest with remains of causeways, reservoirs and homes.

caveat: Temple forms use a simplified Maya profile; not every pyramid stood in a single year.

stages.name: Hill settlement
stages.story: An emerging southern African center develops around hill and valley settlements.

stages.name: Great Enclosure
stages.story: Dry-stone enclosures and far-reaching trade shape the built landscape.

stages.name: Stonework survives
stages.story: The impressive mortarless walls remain, although many earlier buildings were perishable.

caveat: Elliptical walls and tower are schematic; not all enclosures developed simultaneously.

stages.name: Roman street life
stages.story: Before the Roman colony, Pompeii was shaped by Samnite and wider Campanian cultures. The city’s streets and temples developed over generations.

stages.name: The inhabited town
stages.story: Around 70 CE: paved streets, shops, atrium houses, gardens, public baths, the forum and amphitheater made this a bustling Roman city.

stages.name: Eruption of 79 CE
stages.story: In 79 CE pumice and ash accumulated; roofs collapsed, then lethal pyroclastic currents reached the city. The eruption was not a lava flood. This view is an evocative cross-section, not an eyewitness reconstruction.

caveat: Stylized city blocks, amphitheater, forum and domus atria follow known Roman urban forms, not a mapped street-by-street survey. Ash is a representation of 79 CE fallout, not lava.

stages.name: Flavian building works
stages.story: The Flavian Amphitheatre is constructed during the reigns of Vespasian and Titus.

stages.name: Amphitheatre opens
stages.story: Its opening as an arena forms part of imperial spectacle and civic life.

stages.name: Layered ruins
stages.story: Centuries of change leave a partially surviving amphitheatre in a living city.

caveat: An elliptical arena with simplified arcades represents the Colosseum; precise arch counts are not reconstructed.

stages.name: Earlier frontier works
stages.story: Centuries of frontier fortification precede many of the wall sectors seen today.

stages.name: Ming fortifications
stages.story: Ming-era walls and watchtowers redefine sections of the defensive network.

stages.name: Surviving wall sectors
stages.story: Preserved, restored and eroded stretches vary greatly; no single wall condition represents all of China.

caveat: A winding Ming-style stretch is representative, not a continuously accurate Great Wall map.

stages.name: Foundation and craftspeople
stages.story: Craft workers begin the Mughal mausoleum commissioned by Shah Jahan.

stages.name: Marble mausoleum
stages.story: The main white marble mausoleum is completed; other garden and gateway works continue.

stages.name: Conserved masterpiece
stages.story: The Taj remains a carefully conserved monument within its riverside garden.

caveat: Dome, minarets and garden axes are stylized, not a survey-level monument.

stages.name: Cutting into the cliff
stages.story: Rock-cut works are associated with the reign of Ramesses II; exact building years are approximate.

stages.name: Ramesside sanctuary
stages.story: A monumental temple facade is carved into sandstone beside the Nile landscape.

stages.name: Relocated temple
stages.story: The monuments were relocated during the 1960s to protect them from rising Lake Nasser.

caveat: Seated statues and cliff are schematic; the scene does not show exact relocation engineering.

stages.name: Rock landscape
stages.story: The massive rock outcrop has a longer religious and settlement history.

stages.name: Palace & gardens
stages.story: A late fifth-century royal complex develops with gardens and architecture around the rock.

stages.name: Monastic and heritage site
stages.story: Rock, water gardens and surviving foundations remain; detailed palace rooflines are hypothetical.

caveat: Rock shape and summit structures are illustrative, not lidar terrain.

stages.name: Early Indus settlement
stages.story: The urban center grows during the Mature Harappan period.

stages.name: Planned urban blocks
stages.story: Brick-built blocks, drains and the Great Bath point to sophisticated city engineering.

stages.name: Excavated street grid
stages.story: Excavated remains show parts of a much larger settlement; its population is uncertain.

caveat: Street blocks and bathing pool are symbolic, not an accurate excavation plan.

stages.name: Highland rock landscape
stages.story: The highland religious landscape develops around the medieval Zagwe period.

stages.name: Rock-hewn churches
stages.story: Monolithic churches are cut down into rock and connected by trenches and passages.

stages.name: Living pilgrimage
stages.story: The churches remain places of worship and ongoing conservation.

caveat: One cruciform rock-cut church is schematic; exact carving sequence is debated.

stages.name: Darius begins a terrace
stages.story: Darius I begins a major terrace and royal construction project.

stages.name: Achaemenid palace complex
stages.story: Columns, stairways and halls express successive Achaemenid royal programs.

stages.name: Ruined monumental terrace
stages.story: Column remains and stone reliefs survive after ancient destruction and later decay.

caveat: Column grid and gates stand in for a larger palace ensemble; roofs are hypothetical.

stages.name: Inca highland capital
stages.story: The Cusco region is shaped by earlier settlements and emerging Inca institutions.

stages.name: Terraced fortress walls
stages.story: Massive zigzag walls at Saqsaywaman express extraordinary stone-cutting skill.

stages.name: Living city & stonework
stages.story: Stonework survives within a complex living Andean city and landscape.

caveat: Wall alignment is emblematic only; the model is not an excavated architectural plan.
